The entire Famima Coffee set up/machine/sourcing is co-developed by Japanese World Brewer's Cup champion Tetsu Kasuya, who is basically the James Hoffmann of Japan. 

There's a lot of science and interesting method that goes into producing the coffee at convenience stores. Tetsu Kasuya did a whole deep dive/taste test of the different konbini coffee ranges on his channel! Not the canned coffee by the way, the coffee machine coffee. Very much worth a watch!

Thank you for doing this video. My 21 year old son just returned from a two week trip to Japan. Thanks to your video I got to see the convenience stores he went to. This was so cool for me! I thought it was neat that you compared and ranked these foods. It’s good there’s a variety of foods in the convenience stores, must be very helpful for students and people short n time to cook a quick little meal. He brought back lots of awesome gifts and I now have a keychain from Family Mart of a collaboration of an artist, it’s four little coffee cups with Famima Cafe on them. And yes, my kid bought socks, too, from the convenience stores. Thank you!

The food everywhere in Japan is amazing.  If you are an adventurous eater but traveling with non-adventurous eaters, combini foods and snacks are a lifesaver.  I like the bento set from Lawson the best.  I ate so many onigiri while there this summer, and now I stock one or two in my fridg when I have leftover short grain rice from another recipe (mix with bonito flakes, soy, mirin, sugar - press - done!).  I try to make more things I can serve in little dishes and spicy refrigerator pickles for appetizers are my new jam.

Now you need to come to Hawaii and try our convenience store food. Our 7-11s are owned by the Japanese chain, so we have musubi, and a lot of other foods you don’t get on the mainland, they even just started carrying a Japanese style tamago sando. We also have a Korean chain now, CU.
